questions.q: When checking the finished report suite against Lesson 38's scope, what determines whether the project is actually complete?
options: Every piece (summary report, parameters, drillthrough, detail report) does what was originally scoped — not whether it has extra features
Whether the suite has more charts than any other student's project
Whether the summary report can query every table in AdventureWorksDW2014 at once
Whether the video narration has been recorded
questions.explain: Completeness here means matching the original scope piece by piece — the same discipline this catalog's other capstone-wrap-up lessons use, not adding unscoped features.

questions.q: When presenting the suite, what should come first — the problem statement or the implementation details?
options: A one-sentence statement of the problem, before walking through the summary report, the drillthrough, and the detail report
The full text of the drillthrough action's parameter-mapping dialog
A list of every SSRS keyboard shortcut used while building it
The exact render time in milliseconds of the most recent preview
questions.explain: Leading with a plain-language problem statement, then the summary report, then the drillthrough, then the detail report, is the order that actually communicates what the suite demonstrates.

questions.q: Why does the guide say to be ready to explain WHY OrderDetailByTerritory's parameters are Internal, specifically?
options: Because that design decision is a fair proxy for whether you understand report-to-report navigation, not just Report Builder's UI
Because interviewers only ever ask about parameter data types
Because Internal parameters are optional and could be removed with no effect
Because SSRS requires every parameter on every report to be Internal
questions.explain: Explaining that design decision shows real understanding of why a detail report meant only for drillthrough shouldn't prompt a user directly — not just familiarity with checking a box in a dialog.

questions.q: Which course does this lesson point to as the next logical step in the catalog?
options: Data Modeling & Data Warehousing
Blockchain Development
Advanced Excel for Data Analysts
There are no further courses recommended
questions.explain: Data Modeling & Data Warehousing goes deeper into the star-schema design decisions behind AdventureWorksDW2014 that this capstone only relied on, not designed from scratch.

questions.q: What should a portfolio-ready description of this project include, according to the lesson?
options: Both kept .rdl files and a short README describing the databases and architecture — an inspectable artifact, not just a resume line
Only a screenshot of the Report Builder ribbon
A video of the drillthrough being clicked, with no other documentation
Nothing — paginated reports can't be shown to anyone outside the company that built them
questions.explain: A resume sentence alone can't be verified; keeping both actual .rdl files plus a README describing the two databases and the architecture table turns this into something a reviewer can actually inspect.
